To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the data-driven approach is effective in discovering the speech act taxonomy for educational games, that the data-driven taxonomy is more fine-grained and that it has higher accuracy than the extrinsic taxonomy.
the data-driven clustering approach to speech act classification outperforms the expert-driven approach in all three datasets.

(i) we have presented a data-driven approach for automatically discovering the speech acts taxonomy in a dialogue-based educational game, which has been validated using three datasets from three games, and (ii) the discovered taxonomy was found to be consistent with human experts’ intuitional taxonomy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Can speech acts in educational games be discovered automatically?
discovering the speech act categories from a corpus of utterances, which can then be used to classify the utterances in that corpus.
the following question: Can we build a speech act taxonomy that combines both extrinsic (intuition-driven) and intrinsic (data-driven) aspects of the target domain?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data-driven method presented in this work is a promising step towards the discovery of speech act taxonomies that are both data-driven and expert-informed.
the proposed approach can be used to automatically discover speech act categories in multi-party educational games and the resulting taxonomies are comparable to the taxonomies defined by experts.
the intrinsic approach is not yet mature enough for real-world applications, and that the extrinsic approach is still necessary.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a data-driven approach to discovering speech act categories in educational games.
the intrinsic taxonomy discovered by the clustering algorithm was more consistent with the human-annotated taxonomy, which is the first time that this result has been reported.
the data-driven speech act taxonomy is more fine-grained than the expert-driven taxonomy, and that the data-driven taxonomy can capture more subtle speech act distinctions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a purely data-driven approach to discovering speech act categories can yield promising results.
the intrinsic speech act taxonomy can be discovered from dialogue data, and the resulting taxonomy is similar to the taxonomy designed by the experts.
speech act categories are not universal across all educational games and that a data-driven method can discover game specific categories.
